text:
Marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small service we tentatively call the "compat-curator" to centralize deprecation/tombstone metadata and signals. It would be the canonical source of truth and push notifications to gateways/sidecars. Thoughts?

Oliver: +1 on centralizing the metadata. Main worry: coupling runtime to a network lookup on every request. If curator is down, we don't want global fail-open surprises.

Priya: Also need to define how we communicate the deprecation window to clients. Headers? Events in the Console? We should attach a deprecation id so rollouts can be tracked.

Sam: Prefer soft-deprecation first. Emit an "X-Compat-Deprecation" header with structured info, e.g. id, sunset-ts, recommended replacement. Clients can log and adapt. Avoid hard 410 for a grace period. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Marta: Agreed on header + id. Example header payload (HTTP response header JSON encoded):

```
X-Compat-Deprecation: {"id":"dep-2024-11-model-v1","sunset":"2025-01-15T00:00:00Z","replacement":"/v2/generate","action":"migrate"}
```

Oliver: Implementation suggestion: curator exposes a publish-only API + webhook fanout. Gateways implement a local cache and subscribe to webhooks for invalidation. That avoids per-request remote calls.

Priya: Telemetry: curator should emit metrics: total requests flagged, unique tenants affected, time-to-migrate histogram. We want an automatic alert if >5% of traffic hits tombstoned semantics after cutoff.

Sam: Runtime concerns: caching TTLs, CDN propagation, and KV cache semantics for chat/stateful flows. If gateway caches a deprecation flag for a path, ensure we version the cache key by deprecation id to avoid stale mixing of responses. Local memcache + etag-based invalidation is OK.

Jen: Who owns the adapters that transform curator signals into gateway behavior? Is that eng-platform or ops? Need clear ownership to avoid bikeshedding.

Oliver: My vote: architecture owns the curator schema and API contract; eng-platform owns the gateway adapters and rollout automation; eng-infra owns CDN/invalidation playbooks. That splits responsibilities cleanly.

Priya: Avoid query param-based fallbacks (e.g., ?compat=legacy). CDNs tend to cache and leak those. Prefer header-based opt-out or tenant-scoped feature flag.

Sam: Also recommend a "grace" mode where gateways can auto-translate requests to replacement endpoints for a short period (configurable per-deprecation) to reduce customer breakage during migration.

Marta: Proposed rollout plan (high level):
1) v0.1 curator API + schema PR (arch)
2) eng-platform implements adapter + local cache + integration tests
3) canary push to small tenant cohort with header emission only (no hard reject) week 1
4) extend to 50% traffic with auto-translate grace layer week 2
5) enable migration alerts and ramp to 100% week 3
6) set tombstone enforcement (hard 410) at week 4 if >95% migrated

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: compat-curator v0.1 canary -> 2024-11-02T03:00:00Z (canary window 24h) :rocket:

Oliver: Adding integration test checklist: simulate stale client hitting tombstoned path, verify header emitted, verify adapter auto-translate when enabled, verify metrics emitted to Console. I'll create test tickets in eng-platform.

Jen: One ops question: if we schedule hard tombstone, do we also keep a short-lived shim service for enterprise customers who request more time? Need a support path documented.

Priya: Yes — support path should exist but be gated: manual ticket, tenant-scoped feature flag allowing extra 30 days, tracked in curator metadata. Make sure we emit per-tenant telemetry so we don't hide risk.

Sam: Small nit: ensure the curator API responses are idempotent and versioned (v1/v2). Gateways should tolerate unknown fields. Backwards tolerant parsing is key.

Marta: Summary / decision: architecture will own the curator API and schema; eng-platform will implement adapters; eng-infra handles CDN/invalidation; eng-customer-success + support will get a short doc PR for the tenant grace process. I'll write up RFC appendix and open a PR to the design repo today. :thumbsup:

Jen: Thanks — please @me on the PR so we can slot the ops runbook.

Oliver: Noted — I'll start the eng-platform test scaffolding after PR lands.

Marta: Great. I'll post the RFC appendix link when the PR is in.

deploy-bot: Note: compat-curator v0.1 canary deployed (canary id c-773) — monitor metric curator.deprecations.emitted :eyes:

Sam: ack, watching the metric.

Priya: leaving a reminder: no query-param fallbacks, prefer header + tenant flag.

Marta: Perfect — thanks all.
